entries.finding: An updated 2025 meta-analysis of nine randomized trials involving 501 participants found curcumin significantly improved global cognitive function versus placebo.
In the 2025 curcumin cognition analysis, pooled cognitive benefit was significant in studies lasting at least 24 weeks, indicating duration is an important evidence boundary.
The 2025 subgroup analysis found significant cognitive benefit among participants aged 60 years or older, so the strongest signal should not automatically be generalized to younger adults.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of eight randomized trials involving 567 participants found curcumin improved pooled anxiety symptom scores, but heterogeneity was very high and higher-quality confirmation was recommended.
The pooled curcumin anxiety result had very high between-study heterogeneity, so the direction of the signal should be separated from confidence in a uniform clinical effect.

A 2025 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 82 randomized trials involving 5,026 participants found Nigella sativa supplementation improved multiple cardiovascular and metabolic risk markers, but interventions ranged widely in dose, form, and duration.

The 2025 Nigella sativa synthesis reported improvements in fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, postprandial glucose, and QUICKI, but these are pooled surrogate outcomes rather than evidence that Nigella treats diabetes as a disease.

The 2025 meta-analysis found pooled improvements in systolic and diastolic blood pressure with Nigella sativa supplementation, while emphasizing the broad range of interventions represented in the evidence base.

A 2025 systematic review of 15 pediatric clinical trials reported no statistically significant increase in side effects with Nigella sativa, but pediatric evidence remains limited and doses and forms varied substantially.

The 2025 pediatric review concluded more high-quality studies are needed to establish effective pediatric doses, formulations, and indications; absence of a significant pooled safety signal is not proof of established pediatric safety.

A 2025 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 29 randomized trials found ginger supplementation reduced CRP, TNF-alpha, and IL-6 concentrations versus control, alongside improvements in several oxidative-stress markers.

The 2025 ginger synthesis found increased total antioxidant capacity and superoxide dismutase activity and reduced malondialdehyde, indicating biomarker-level antioxidant effects rather than direct proof of prevention or treatment of a specific disease.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of 35 randomized trials found ginger capsules used alongside standard antiemetic therapy reduced some measures of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting; the evidence included different ginger formulations and should not be generalized to every ginger product.
